h1: The 7 Best NVMe Enclosures Under $100 of 2026, Ranked & Reviewed
metaTitle: Best NVMe Enclosures Under $100: Ranked & Reviewed
metaDescription: Ranked and reviewed by Primea: 7 NVMe enclosures under $100, compared on 10, 20 and 40Gbps links, cooling fans, dual-bay cloning and tool-free installation.
summary: The UGREEN 40Gbps enclosure is the best NVMe case under $100 for most people who already own a drive and a 40Gbps port. The ORICO 40Gbps adds a cooling fan, the ANYOYO pairs 40Gbps with a fan and a dual-chip design, and the ORICO dual-bay clones drives without a PC. The ACASIS 10Gbps and ASUS ROG Arion suit slower ports.
intro: A fast enclosure only pays off if the port, the cable and the drive all keep up. A 40Gbps enclosure plugged into a 10Gbps laptop port runs at 10Gbps, and an old drive may not saturate even that. The number on the box sets a ceiling, and the cheapest way to waste money is to buy a ceiling you cannot reach.

We ranked seven NVMe enclosures, all in the $50 to $100 bracket, on the Primea framework, scoring link speed, cooling and the installation experience. The spec sheets are short, giving link speeds and headline features but few thermal or controller details, so we flag the gaps rather than guess at them.

products.name: UGREEN 40Gbps M.2 NVMe Enclosure (SSD Not Included)
products.verdict: A 40Gbps enclosure with a dedicated heat-dissipation design, sold without the SSD.
products.description:
UGREEN pitches this 40Gbps enclosure as quick for large transfers, with a unique heat dissipation design and support for multiple SSD types. The SSD is not included, which is the norm.

It wins by being the cleanest option at this speed: the cooling is built into the shell rather than relying on a small fan that can fail or whine. The ORICO and ANYOYO models use fans, which move more air but add moving parts.

Buy it if your laptop or desktop has a 40Gbps port and you own a spare drive. The caveat is that the listing gives few thermal details, so if you plan multi-hour copies of very large files, watch the case temperature by touch and let it rest between jobs.
products.idealFor: Buyers who have a spare NVMe drive and a 40Gbps port.
products.skipIf: Your computer only has a 10Gbps port.

products.name: ORICO 40Gbps M.2 NVMe SSD Enclosure with Built-in Cooling Fan
products.verdict: 40Gbps with multiple heat-dissipation measures and a built-in cooling fan.
products.description:
ORICO lists 40Gbps speed, multiple heat dissipation methods, wide compatibility and a built-in cooling fan.

The fan is the difference from the UGREEN: it keeps a fast drive from throttling during long copies of video files. It ranks second because a fan adds noise and a wear item, while the UGREEN's passive design has neither.

Buy it for heavy sustained transfers. The caveat is fan noise, which the listing does not quantify, so it may not suit a silent desk, and a fan that clogs with dust will need an occasional blast of compressed air.
products.idealFor: Users moving large video or backup files who worry about throttling.

products.name: ANYOYO 40Gbps M.2 NVMe SSD Enclosure with Cooling Fan
products.verdict: A 40Gbps fan-cooled enclosure with a dual-chip design aimed at stability.
products.description:
ANYOYO lists 40Gbps transfer, a cooling fan, dual-chip reliability and superior heat dissipation.

It ranks third because the dual-chip claim is a selling point without detail: the listing does not say which chips or how they work. It matches the ORICO on speed and cooling and trails it only in recognizability.

Buy it if the price is right and you want a fan. The caveat is the vague chip description. Without a named controller you cannot check driver support or firmware updates, so read buyer questions on the listing before you commit to it for important backups.
products.idealFor: Buyers who want a fan-cooled 40Gbps case and are open to a newer brand.

products.name: Yottamaster M.2 NVMe SSD Enclosure 40Gbps
products.verdict: A 40Gbps enclosure with a clear tool-free installation design.
products.description:
Yottamaster offers 40Gbps speed, wide compatibility and tool-free installation with a clear design.

The tool-free install is the draw: you can swap drives without a screwdriver, handy if you move one drive between machines. It ranks fourth because no cooling feature is listed, and sustained transfers on a fast drive generate heat.

Buy it for easy drive swaps. The caveat is the lack of a stated cooling design, so long transfers may slow as the drive warms, and a clear shell does nothing to move heat away from the controller.
products.idealFor: People who swap drives often and want no tools.

products.name: ORICO 20Gbps Dual Bay NVMe Enclosure Tool-Free M.2 NVMe Enclosure
products.verdict: Two tool-free bays, 20Gbps, silent passive cooling and PC-free offline cloning.
products.description:
Two bays share a 20Gbps link, with tool-free installation, 0dB silent passive cooling and a one-key offline clone that works between two drives without a PC.

Offline cloning is the unique feature: you can copy a drive to another without a computer in the middle. It ranks fifth because 20Gbps is shared by two bays and slower than the 40Gbps single-bay cases.

Buy it if cloning is the goal. The caveat is that the same-protocol clone requires matching drives, and the destination must be at least as large as the source, so plan your capacities before you buy a second drive.
products.idealFor: Buyers who clone drives or run two NVMe drives at once.

products.name: ASUS ROG Strix Arion Aluminum Alloy M.2 NVMe SSD Enclosure Case Adapter
products.verdict: An aluminum alloy case on USB Type-C 3.2 with two cables included.
products.description:
The ROG Strix Arion is an aluminum alloy enclosure for M.2 PCIe NVMe drives, using USB Type-C 3.2 and including two cables.

It ranks sixth because the link speed is not listed beyond the USB 3.2 label, and the 40Gbps cases are clearly faster in their listings. The metal body and included cables are real benefits.

Buy it for a brand name and a metal body. The caveat is that speed is less clearly stated, so compare it to a 40Gbps case only if your port is slower anyway, and keep the two cables handy for desktops and laptops alike.
products.idealFor: Buyers who want a known brand and a metal body for everyday storage.

products.name: ACASIS 10Gbps Magnetic M.2 NVMe SSD Enclosure with 4K ProRes Recording
products.verdict: A 10Gbps magnetic enclosure with a cooling fan, aimed at 4K@60 video recording.
products.description:
The ACASIS runs at 10Gbps, attaches magnetically, has a cooling fan and is marketed for 4K@60 ProRes storage.

It ranks last because 10Gbps is the slowest link here, but the magnetic mount and fan suit a phone-recording workflow. It is a niche product for content creators.

Buy it for recording to a phone. The caveat is that magnetic attachment depends on your device, so check that your phone or case supports it, and confirm that the fan does not add noise to your recordings.
products.idealFor: Creators who record video straight to an external SSD.
products.skipIf: You want a general-purpose fast case.

whatMatters.detail: A 40Gbps enclosure needs a 40Gbps port to run at full speed. On a 10Gbps port it will run at 10Gbps. Check your computer's port speed before paying for a faster case. If your port is 10Gbps, the ACASIS or ASUS is enough. Also check the cable: a slow cable quietly caps a fast enclosure, so use the one in the box.

NVMe drives slow down when hot. Passive designs, such as the UGREEN or the ORICO dual-bay, are silent, while fans on the ORICO 40Gbps, ANYOYO and ACASIS move more air at the cost of noise. Match cooling to how long your transfers run, and remember that a case sitting on a soft surface traps heat whatever the spec says.

If you swap drives often, a tool-free design saves time and avoids losing tiny screws. The Yottamaster and ORICO dual-bay list it. Otherwise a screw-in design is fine for a drive you install once. Check the listing photos to see how the drive is held, because a loose drive can flex and wear the connector.

A dual-bay case holds two drives and can clone one to the other without a PC. The ORICO dual-bay does this with one key. The catch is that the 20Gbps link is shared, so each drive gets less than a single-bay 40Gbps case.

Enclosures support M.2 NVMe, and some also support SATA. Check the listing for the drive type, and note that the SSD is usually not included. Confirm the length of M.2 drive supported if you use a long drive, since not every listing states the supported length, and ask the seller when in doubt.

faq.q: Does the enclosure include an SSD?
faq.a: No. The UGREEN is explicitly sold without an SSD, and the others are enclosures only. You add your own M.2 NVMe drive. Check the listing for the supported drive length before you buy.
Buying 40Gbps for a 10Gbps port. The UGREEN or ORICO will run at your port's speed. Check your laptop's port first, and save money with the ACASIS or ASUS if the port is slower.

faq.q: Is the ORICO 40Gbps worth it over the UGREEN?
faq.a: Only if you do long transfers. The ORICO adds a cooling fan, while the UGREEN uses passive heat dissipation. For everyday use the UGREEN's silent design is simpler.

faq.q: How do I install the drive?
faq.a: Open the case, seat the M.2 drive in the slot, and close it. The Yottamaster and ORICO dual-bay are tool-free, so no screwdriver is needed. Format the drive on first use.

faq.q: How do I keep the drive cool?
faq.a: Keep the enclosure in open air, away from soft surfaces. Fan models like the ANYOYO need clear intake. Avoid stacking devices on a passive case such as the UGREEN.

faq.q: Can the ORICO dual-bay clone without a computer?
faq.a: Yes, through its one-key offline clone, as long as both drives use the same protocol. This works without a PC. For regular transfers to a computer, a single-bay 40Gbps case is faster.

finalTake: The UGREEN 40Gbps M.2 NVMe Enclosure (SSD Not Included) is the best NVMe enclosure under $100 for most people with a fast port. The ORICO 40Gbps with a fan suits sustained transfers, the ORICO dual-bay handles cloning, and the Yottamaster is the tool-free choice. Match the enclosure to your port speed first.
